title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #16

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which part of a bean plant grows in the soil? (1 mark)
   A. Pods
   B. Leaves
   C. Flowers
   D. Roots

2. Which is the best way of studying how a seedling grows? (1 mark)
   A. Never water it
   B. Measure its height every two days
   C. Pull it up daily
   D. Cover it in sand

3. Which part of the plant is usually flat, green and spread out to catch light? (1 mark)
   A. Seed
   B. Leaf
   C. Root
   D. Stem

4. Which of these can you use to find out the differences between vertebrates and invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Noise
   B. Weather
   C. Books and digital sources
   D. Only guesses

5. Which of these is a good way to care for a farm animal? (1 mark)
   A. Give it dirty water
   B. Give clean water and shelter
   C. Beat it
   D. Leave it in the rain

6. Which of these helps to keep teeth healthy? (1 mark)
   A. Never visiting a dentist
   B. Biting hard objects
   C. Eating many sweets
   D. Brushing twice a day

7. What is constipation? (1 mark)
   A. Passing hard, dry faeces with difficulty
   B. Having worms
   C. Passing watery faeces
   D. Vomiting

8. Where does digestion finish and digested food pass into the blood? (1 mark)
   A. Mouth
   B. Small intestine
   C. Stomach
   D. Rectum

9. What is vomiting? (1 mark)
   A. Passing loose faeces
   B. Chewing food
   C. Food coming out through the mouth
   D. Feeling hungry

10. Which of these is a healthy habit for digestion? (1 mark)
   A. Eating food that fell in dirt
   B. Never washing fruits
   C. Drinking water from a dirty pond
   D. Washing hands before eating

11. What does mass mean? (1 mark)
   A. How hot an object is
   B. How bright an object is
   C. The amount of matter in an object
   D. The space an object takes up

12. How many millilitres are in 1 litre? (1 mark)
   A. 10 000
   B. 100
   C. 1000
   D. 10

13. Which of these is a reason we need gases? (1 mark)
   A. We can write with them
   B. We breathe air
   C. We can build houses with them
   D. We can sit on them

14. Why should each child use their own balloon for the balloon activity? (1 mark)
   A. To make it burst
   B. To avoid spreading germs
   C. To make it heavier
   D. To make the balloon bigger

15. How many grams are in 1 kilogram? (1 mark)
   A. 100
   B. 10
   C. 500
   D. 1000

16. Which grouping of gases is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Air, steam and cooking gas are gases
   B. Milk, chalk and steam are solids
   C. Sugar, oil and air are solids
   D. Stone, water and wood are liquids

17. Which of these is e-waste? (1 mark)
   A. An old phone
   B. A paper bag
   C. A banana peel
   D. A leaf

18. At a wedding, what can organisers do to keep the place clean? (1 mark)
   A. Provide bins and clean after the event
   B. Leave waste on the ground
   C. Burn plastic
   D. Throw waste in a river

19. Which living things help waste to decompose? (1 mark)
   A. Bottles
   B. Plastic bags
   C. Fungi and bacteria
   D. Stones

20. Which of these is NOT a way to conserve water? (1 mark)
   A. Washing dishes under a running tap
   B. Using a basin
   C. Harvesting rainwater
   D. Fixing leaks

21. Which reused water is safe for drinking? (1 mark)
   A. Water that washed vegetables
   B. Water that washed clothes
   C. Water that washed a car
   D. None of the used washing water

22. What should you do when you see a leaking tap at school? (1 mark)
   A. Play with it
   B. Tell an adult so it can be fixed
   C. Ignore it
   D. Open it wider

23. A tap leaks 3 litres each hour. How much is wasted in one day of 24 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 48 litres
   B. 27 litres
   C. 24 litres
   D. 72 litres

24. Which of these is a source of fresh water? (1 mark)
   A. The sea
   B. A salty lake only
   C. A river
   D. A puddle of sea water

25. A flash of light in the sky during a storm is a natural source of light. What is it? (1 mark)
   A. A car headlight
   B. Lightning
   C. A solar lamp
   D. A lantern

26. Which of these is a benefit of good lighting when reading? (1 mark)
   A. It makes letters disappear
   B. It prevents tired eyes
   C. It makes pages smell
   D. It makes books heavier

27. Which of these is a fuel? (1 mark)
   A. Glass
   B. Sand
   C. Firewood
   D. Clean water

28. Which of these is the biggest natural source of heat for the Earth? (1 mark)
   A. A fire
   B. An iron
   C. A kettle
   D. The sun

29. What should you never do with oil that is on fire? (1 mark)
   A. Call for help
   B. Pour water on it
   C. Move away
   D. Cover it with a lid

30. Why do wet clothes dry faster in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. The sun makes water colder
   B. The sun makes them heavy
   C. The heat evaporates the water
   D. The sun adds water

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain why deworming is important and state two other ways of preventing worms. (4 marks)

32. Group these into solid, liquid and gas: milk, chalk, oxygen, cooking oil, book, steam. (4 marks)

33. Describe the characteristics that show that animals are living things. Use examples. (5 marks)

34. Give three ways of lighting a house at night. (3 marks)

35. A pupil wants to find out which material is transparent, translucent or opaque. Describe a test. (4 marks)

36. Name two ways of lighting a house during the day. (2 marks)

37. Describe how solid waste causes flooding in towns. (4 marks)

38. Name the parts of the digestive system in the order food passes through them. (2 marks)

39. Describe safety measures to be observed when handling heat at home and at school. (5 marks)

40. A tap leaks 4 litres every hour. How much water is lost in 6 hours? (2 marks)

41. Explain why a football is described as a container of matter although it looks empty. (3 marks)

42. What is a force? Give one example of a push and one example of a pull. (2 marks)

43. Explain why light is important in our daily lives. (5 marks)

44. Explain why plants are called living things. (3 marks)

45. Give two ways in which animals are different from plants. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Roots
   Roots grow underground.

2. B — Measure its height every two days
   Measuring height regularly shows growth over time.

3. B — Leaf
   The flat, green shape of a leaf helps it catch light.

4. C — Books and digital sources
   We can search print and digital media for information.

5. B — Give clean water and shelter
   Farm animals need water, food, shelter and care.

6. D — Brushing twice a day
   Brushing removes food remains and prevents tooth decay.

7. A — Passing hard, dry faeces with difficulty
   Constipation means hard faeces that are difficult to pass.

8. B — Small intestine
   The small intestine completes digestion and absorbs food into the blood.

9. C — Food coming out through the mouth
   Vomiting is throwing up food through the mouth.

10. D — Washing hands before eating
   Clean hands prevent germs from entering the mouth.

11. C — The amount of matter in an object
   Mass is the amount of matter in something.

12. C — 1000
   1 litre is 1000 ml.

13. B — We breathe air
   Air gives us oxygen for breathing.

14. B — To avoid spreading germs
   Sharing a balloon that has been in someone's mouth can spread germs.

15. D — 1000
   1 kg is 1000 g.

16. A — Air, steam and cooking gas are gases
   Air, steam and cooking gas are gases.

17. A — An old phone
   E-waste means old electrical and electronic items.

18. A — Provide bins and clean after the event
   Bins and cleaning keep the place tidy.

19. C — Fungi and bacteria
   Decomposers such as fungi and bacteria break down waste.

20. A — Washing dishes under a running tap
   A running tap wastes water.

21. D — None of the used washing water
   Used washing water is not safe to drink.

22. B — Tell an adult so it can be fixed
   Reporting leaks helps save water.

23. D — 72 litres
   3 x 24 = 72 litres.

24. C — A river
   Rivers carry fresh water that people can use.

25. B — Lightning
   Lightning is a natural flash of light.

26. B — It prevents tired eyes
   Enough light makes reading easier.

27. C — Firewood
   Fuels burn to give heat.

28. D — The sun
   The sun heats the Earth.

29. B — Pour water on it
   Water on burning oil spreads the fire.

30. C — The heat evaporates the water
   Heat makes water turn to vapour.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Worms live in the intestines and take food and make us weak. Deworming kills them. Wear shoes, wash hands, keep nails short.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 1 mark each for other ways.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Solids: chalk and book. Liquids: milk and cooking oil. Gases: oxygen and steam.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

33. (5 marks)
   Answer: Animals feed, grow, breathe, reproduce, remove waste, move, respond and die. Give examples such as a goat eating grass and a hen laying eggs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sign to a maximum of 5.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Electric bulbs, solar lamps, paraffin lamps, candles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Use a torch in a dark room. Put tissue paper, clear plastic and a book one at a time between the torch and a wall. Record whether all, some or no light passes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for equipment, 1 mark for method, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for classification.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: Windows and translucent roof sheets (skylights).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Polythene bags and plastic block drains. Water cannot flow away when it rains. It gathers in the streets and floods homes and roads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 4.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, anus.
   Working / marking points: Award 2 marks for the correct order. 1 mark if at most two parts are out of order.

39. (5 marks)
   Answer: Do not play with matches, keep children from fires, use gloves, turn handles inwards, switch off cookers and irons, keep fuels away from fire, cool burns with water and tell an adult.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each measure up to 5.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: 24 litres.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 4 x 6 and 1 mark for the answer with units.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is full of air. Air is a gas, so it has mass and takes up space. It keeps the ball in shape.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for air inside, 1 mark for air being matter, 1 mark for it filling the ball.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: A force is a push or a pull. A push: kicking a ball. A pull: opening a drawer.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for the two examples.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: It lets us see, keeps us safe, helps plants to make food, dries clothes, gives solar power and discourages pests.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 5.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: They show signs of life. They grow, reproduce, remove waste, respond to changes and die.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying they show signs of life and 2 marks for correct signs given.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Animals can move from place to place. Animals feed on ready-made food while plants make their own.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct difference.
